title: Domain and range of a function
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:21Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, mat-domain-range, teaches the same idea but at Year 11 depth, using square-root and fraction domain restrictions that go beyond what a Years 9 and 10 Stage 5 path would need, so it is not a suitable match.

draft.title: Domain and range of a function
card: every \(x\) value the function allows as an input.
every \(y\) value the function produces as an output.
From a rule: a function such as \(\frac{1}{x}\) cannot divide by zero, so \(x \ne 0\). A function such as \(\sqrt{x}\) needs \(x \ge 0\).
Worked example: for \(y = x^{2} + 1\), any \(x\) works, so the domain is all real numbers. As \(x^{2} \ge 0\), we get \(y \ge 1\), so the range is \(y \ge 1\).
draft.remember: Domain is the allowed inputs, \(x\). Range is the outputs produced, \(y\).

a.why: The square root of a negative number is not a real number, so \(x\) must be 0 or more. \(y \ge 0\) is the range, not the domain, since it lists outputs.
a.clue: Which \(x\) values give a real square root?

b.q: What is the range of \(y = x^{2} - 3\)?
b.why: Since \(x^{2} \ge 0\), the smallest output is \(0 - 3 = -3\), and outputs grow without limit. All real numbers is the domain, not the range, because \(y\) can never go below \(-3\).
b.clue: Find the smallest value \(x^{2}\) can take.
